title: Build a toy kernel with a system call table
brief: Write the handlers and trap dispatcher of a toy kernel that validates user requests and returns negative errno codes, then make two real system calls through a pipe.
hints: A failed system call returns a negative errno number: `-EBADF`, `-EFAULT`, and so on. `errno_name(-9)` gives `"EBADF"`, and a non-negative result gives `None`.
`sys_getpid(kernel)` returns `kernel.pid`. `sys_exit(kernel, status)` sets `kernel.exited = True` and stores `status & 0xFF`, because a real exit status is one byte.

In `sys_write`, validate in this order: the file descriptor is a key of `kernel.files` (else `-EBADF`), `count` is not negative (else `-EINVAL`), the range `addr .. addr + count` lies inside `kernel.user_mem` (else `-EFAULT`). Only then copy the bytes.
Copy with `bytes(kernel.user_mem[addr:addr + count])` and extend `kernel.files[fd]`. Return `count`.

`Kernel.syscall` is the trap handler. Look the number up in `self.table`, return `-ENOSYS` if it is missing, return `-EINVAL` if the argument count is wrong, set `self.mode = "kernel"`, call the handler, and put the mode back to `"user"` in a `finally` block.

Count every trap in `self.syscall_count`, even one that fails. For the real part, `os.pipe()` returns `(read_fd, write_fd)`. Close both ends before you return. Writing to a closed descriptor raises `OSError` with `.errno` set, and `errno.errorcode[e.errno]` is the name.
